Rosy Macarons

Served at: Gaudete Sunday

Makes about 24 macaronsPrep 45 minCook 15 min

Rosy Macarons are delicate French almond meringue cookies filled with a fragrant rose-flavored buttercream. They are a festive treat often enjoyed on Gaudete Sunday, a joyful day in Advent marked by the color pink, symbolizing joy and celebration as Christmas approaches.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (100 g) almond flour
  • 1 3/4 cups (200 g) powdered sugar
  • 3 large egg whites, room temperature
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon rose water
  • Pink gel food coloring (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup (120 g) powdered sugar, sifted
  • 1 teaspoon rose water
  • 1 teaspoon heavy cream

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. In a food processor, combine almond flour and powdered sugar; pulse until finely ground. Sift the mixture into a bowl to remove lumps.
  3. In a clean, dry bowl, beat egg whites on medium speed until foamy. Gradually add granulated sugar, increasing speed to high, and beat until stiff, glossy peaks form.
  4. Gently fold the almond flour mixture into the meringue in batches, adding pink gel food coloring if desired, until the batter flows like lava and ribbons fall slowly from the spatula.
  5. Transfer batter to a piping bag fitted with a round tip. Pipe 1-inch (2.5 cm) rounds onto prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 1 inch apart.
  6. Tap the baking sheets firmly on the counter to release air bubbles. Let the piped shells rest at room temperature for 30-40 minutes until a skin forms and they are no longer sticky to the touch.
  7. Bake one sheet at a time for 14-16 minutes, rotating halfway through, until macarons have risen and feet have formed. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.
  8. For the filling, beat softened butter until creamy. Gradually add powdered sugar, rose water, and heavy cream, beating until smooth and fluffy.
  9. Pair macaron shells of similar size. Pipe or spread a small amount of rose buttercream onto one shell, then sandwich with the other.
  10. Refrigerate assembled macarons in an airtight container for 24 hours to mature the flavors before serving.

Tips

  • Use aged egg whites (separated and left covered in the fridge for 24 hours) for better meringue stability.
  • If rose water is unavailable, substitute with a few drops of rose extract but use sparingly as it is more concentrated.
  • For a natural pink color, add a small amount of beetroot powder to the batter instead of food coloring.
